Can a landlord or agent legally demand two years of rent upfront in Lagos or Kwara? We examine the exact statutory provisions under section 4 of the Lagos Tenancy Law 2011 and Kwara State tenancy law, covering advance rent caps, sitting versus new tenants, and the criminal penalties that apply to both landlords and tenants.

claims.text: In Lagos State, section 4 of the Tenancy Law 2011 is an enforceable advance-rent cap that operates asymmetrically between sitting tenants and new tenants.
For a sitting monthly tenant in Lagos, section 4 subsections 1 and 2 provides that a landlord may not demand or receive, and a tenant may not pay, more than six months of rent in advance.
For a sitting yearly tenant in Lagos, section 4 subsections 1 and 2 provides that a landlord may not demand or receive, and a tenant may not pay, more than one year of rent in advance.
For a new or would-be tenant in Lagos, section 4 subsections 3 and 4 provides that a landlord may not demand or receive more than one year of rent in advance, with no six-month branch available.

Under section 4 subsection 5 of the Lagos law, both sides commit an offence: any person who receives or pays rent in excess is liable on conviction to a fine of 100,000 naira or three months imprisonment.
In Kwara State, the statute contains two conflicting provisions regarding advance rent, stating the cap twice with different numbers.
Under section 4 subsection 6 of the Kwara law, it is unlawful to demand or receive more than one year from individual tenants and two years from commercial or institutional tenants.

Under section 35 subsection 6 of the Kwara law, a landlord who demands or receives more than three months from an individual tenant, or twelve months from a commercial or institutional tenant, is guilty of an offence.
Under section 35 subsection 6 of the Kwara law, the penalty for demanding or receiving excess advance rent is a fine of an amount equivalent to the excess of rent received.

Under section 5 subsection 4 of the Kwara law, it is unlawful for anyone, in consideration of the grant, continuance, surrender or giving up of a tenancy, to require or receive any loan or premium, and such payment is recoverable by the tenant and may be deducted from rent.

Under section 35 subsection 5 of the Kwara law, a person who receives a loan or premium contravening the Law, expressly including in relation to advance payment of rent, is liable on summary conviction to a fine of twice the amount received.

Under section 35 subsection 2 of the Kwara law, attempting to or forcibly ejecting a tenant, harassing or molesting a tenant to eject him, harassing a landlord, doing anything calculated to stultify the Law, or failing to comply with an order carries a penalty of 5,000 naira or six months.
Under section 37 subsection 4 of the Lagos law, it is unlawful for a landlord to eject a tenant while an application challenging an unreasonable rent increase is pending.
There is no statutory percentage cap on rent increases in Lagos or anywhere else in Nigeria.
